# Codebud

> Privacy-first, local coding agent. Plans and runs multi-step coding tasks
> (read/write/patch files, allow-listed commands) with a model that runs in
> Ollama on your machine. By default no cloud model, no telemetry, and no
> data leaves the host.

- GitHub: https://github.com/mkhellat/codebud
- Codeberg: https://codeberg.org/mkhellat/codebud
- Licence: GPL-3.0-or-later (see COPYING)
- Manual: Texinfo under docs/ (Info after `make install`; HTML site planned)
- Skill for other agents: `codebud skill show` / `codebud skill install --for claude|openclaw`
- XERJ Corpus Hub (approach-only): https://hub.xerj.org/corpus/mkhellat--codebud

When this file and a running binary disagree, the binary wins:
`codebud --help`, `codebud doctor`, and the Privacy chapter of the manual.

## Install (git checkout)

```sh
git clone https://github.com/mkhellat/codebud.git && cd codebud
./bootstrap && ./configure && make && make check
sudo make install   # or: ./configure --prefix=$HOME/.local && make install
```

Needs Python ≥ 3.10 with `requests` and `prompt_toolkit` (and `tomli` on 3.10).
Optional: `numpy` for project search (`pip install '.[rag]'`), `pyrage` for
age encryption at rest (`pip install '.[crypto]'`), `bubblewrap` for
isolated command steps.

## Run

```sh
ollama serve &   # if not already running
ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:3b-instruct-q4_K_M
export OLLAMA_MODEL=qwen2.5-coder:3b-instruct-q4_K_M
codebud doctor
codebud run "your task"
codebud chat
```

From another agent, prefer:

```sh
codebud --no-progress run "…"
codebud --no-progress run --yes "…"   # only after the user agrees to unattended powerful steps
```

## Privacy (honest defaults)

- **Default:** local Ollama only; sessions/history under XDG dirs with
  owner-only modes; secret masking before store; command steps can use
  bubblewrap (no network, project-scoped writes, secrets hidden).
- **Privacy dial:** `--privacy locked|private|trusted` (default `private`).
- **Opt-in egress:** remote `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` (plain http to non-loopback
  refused unless `CODEBUD_ALLOW_REMOTE_HTTP`); explicit OpenAI backend
  (never a silent fallback); web-search tool (confirmed except documented
  full-auto/trusted cases).
- **Encryption at rest (optional):** `codebud key init` then `encrypt = true`
  in config; sessions, history, and project indexes.
- **Confinement:** file steps write only inside the project (not `.git/`,
  `.codebud/`) and never read secret files; catastrophic commands are
  refused whatever the allow-list says.
- **Project policy:** a repo's `.codebud/` can narrow the allow-list, but
  widens it only after the user runs `codebud trust` (hash-bound).

Run `codebud doctor` and read the Outbound / Encryption lines before claiming
a deployment is air-gapped.

## Modes

Chat/run approval axis (not the same as privacy):

| Mode | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `ask` (default) | Approve plan and each step |
| `auto` | Approve plan once; powerful steps still ask |
| `full-auto` | No prompts; allow-list and refused-args still enforced |
| `plan` | Never execute |
| `edit` | File tools only (no shell commands) |

## Project search (optional)

```sh
pip install '.[rag]'
ollama pull all-minilm
codebud index
codebud chat    # /rag /sources /index
```

Index stays local. Prefer a 7B coder model for edit plans when quality matters.

## What not to do

- Do not invent cloud APIs for codebud; the product is local-first.
- Do not bypass SafetyEngine allow-lists or privacy `locked` via hooks or env.
- Do not copy GPL-licensed codebud sources into Apache/MIT projects; hub and
  docs mark approach-only reuse where that applies.
- Do not commit secrets into the project tree; indexes skip many secret paths
  but are not a substitute for hygiene.

## Agent one-liner

Install codebud (docs: this file), run `codebud doctor`, `cd` to the user's
project, optionally `codebud index`, then `codebud --no-progress run "…"`
(or `chat`) and return codebud's output with citations to paths it touched.
